summary: Replaced unsigned identity cookies and truncating multi-write JSON persistence with generated local credentials, signed expiring sessions and a validated SQLite transaction boundary that coordinates independent processes.

Completed owned idea/comment CRUD, captured-version edits, reference-aware deletion, private projections, desired vote/follow state, atomic notifications and audits, guarded duplicate merges and working admin/moderation controls.
Added preserved form drafts, export/current-value recovery, coordinated pending writes, navigation guards, stable board/roadmap pagination and responsive desktop/narrow layouts.

Preserved original collection JSON and historical documentation; added explicit non-overwriting fictional setup, 59 passing checks, four reviewed captures and nine detailed project-specific learning documents.

checks.environment: Node 22.16.0; Next.js 16.1.6; React 19.2.3; SQLite 3.49.1; Playwright 1.60 Chromium
checks.command: node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs scripts/verify.ts (43 backend/setup, 16 browser; TypeScript; production build; disposable SQLite fixture)

limits: Local single-board credentials and process-local account throttling; no MFA, reset flow, external identity, distributed limits, session revocation or production deployment.

SQLite aggregate uses the experimental Node 22 built-in module, validates and serializes the full document, and is bounded to 16 MiB / 10,000 rows per collection. Original JSON remains unchanged without automatic import.

No durable create/comment idempotency, automatic draft import/merge, merge undo or external notification delivery. Review records after uncertain responses; notifications show newest 100 and detail audits newest 30.
Desktop/narrow Chromium workflows were checked; no comprehensive accessibility audit, power-loss certification or deployment verification.
